data.name: Ranganatha
data.gender_notes: Ranganatha is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who holds the entire cosmos in his form, an aspect of Lord Vishnu. The name Ranganatha carries the meaning “Lord of the Cosmos” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Ranganatha usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the cosmos and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine aspect of the universe, the creator and sustainer of all existence
data.etymology: Ranganatha belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Cosmos.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ranganatha total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ranganatha" is deeply rooted in Hinduism, representing an aspect of Lord Vishnu who is believed to hold the entire cosmos in his form. This aspect of the deity is particularly revered in South Indian temples, notably in the Srirangam Temple in Tamil Nadu, which is one of the largest temples in the world. The worship of Ranganatha has significant cultural exportations, with the iconography and stories associated with this deity influencing art, literature, and traditional practices in Hindu communities around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: "Ranganatha" is a spiritual name, a reminder of the underlying unity and interconnectedness of all things in the universe. In Hinduism, Vishnu is considered the preserver and sustainer of life. The name "Ranganatha" conveys the idea of the Lord cradling the universe in his divine form. By remembering and invoking Ranganatha, devotees seek to deepen their connection with the divine, find solace and peace in the face of life's challenges, and reaffirm their faith in the ultimate cohesion and order that underlies the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ranganatha, meaning the 'Lord of the Wide-Expansive Abode', represents the divine presence in the cosmic dance of creation and destruction, symbolizing infinite love, compassion, and protection.
